back.body: PREPARATION comes BEFORE the tones and DECIDES EVERY OTHER PHASE — everything missing at 3am was missing at the start of the shift · DISPATCH: listen properly; there is often information that should change something before you arrive · EN ROUTE IS PLANNING TIME — roles, equipment, hazards, expectations · ARRIVAL BEGINS WITH SIZE-UP, NOT PATIENT CONTACT · Care → packaging → transport, with the DESTINATION CHOSEN DELIBERATELY by need, protocol and capability · TRANSFER OF CARE = A VERBAL HANDOVER TO EQUAL OR HIGHER TRAINING, NOT COMPLETE UNTIL THEY ACCEPT — a form in a tray is not transfer, and in many systems it is abandonment · POST-RUN IS A REAL PHASE: clean, disinfect, restock, refuel, report · NOT AVAILABLE UNTIL GENUINELY READY
back.why_it_matters: Six minutes later they took a call that needed two of the things on that list.

front.title: Daily readiness
front.summary: Test it, do not look at it

back.body: CHECK EVERY SHIFT, NO EXCEPTIONS · A CHECK IS A TEST, NOT A GLANCE — turn the suction on and LISTEN to it; open the oxygen and WATCH the flow; work the stretcher and HEAR the locks · EQUIPMENT PRESENT AND BROKEN IS WORSE THAN MISSING, because you find out when you were counting on it · CHECK QUANTITIES AND EXPIRY DATES — both FAIL SILENTLY and a quick look never catches them · CHECK THE VEHICLE AS A VEHICLE: fuel, fluids, tyres, lights, brakes, wipers, warning devices · USE THE WRITTEN CHECKLIST — memory skips the SAME item every time and never notices · FIX OR REPORT AND DOCUMENT IT · The check TEACHES YOU WHERE THINGS ARE, so in the dark you reach instead of searching · OXYGEN IS THE CLASSIC — READ THE GAUGE
back.why_it_matters: The cylinder looked exactly the same as a full one. It read half.

back.body: LIGHTS AND SIRENS REQUEST RIGHT OF WAY, THEY DO NOT CREATE IT — permission can be refused, ignored, or NEVER HEARD · DUE REGARD: you remain responsible for driving safely whatever your warning devices are doing, and it is the standard you will be measured against · DRIVERS STOP DEAD, TURN INTO YOU, GO THE WRONG WAY, OR NEVER HEAR YOU — modern cars are sealed, with the windows up and music on · INTERSECTIONS ARE WHERE AMBULANCES CRASH: SLOW DOWN, COVER THE BRAKE, CHANGE THE SIREN TONE (a constant sound becomes background), CLEAR IT LANE BY LANE, MAKE EYE CONTACT · SPEED SAVES ALMOST NOTHING AND COSTS ENORMOUSLY · EVERYONE RESTRAINED, EVERYTHING STOWED — loose kit is a projectile · A CRASH TURNS ONE EMERGENCY INTO SEVERAL
back.why_it_matters: The car that came through the red never braked. She was still looking straight ahead.

front.title: Roadway safety
front.summary: Set up for the worst driver

back.body: ROADWAY INCIDENTS ARE AMONG THE MOST DANGEROUS THINGS EMS DOES — responders are struck and killed on ordinary calls · PARK TO PROTECT THE WORKING AREA, NOT FOR AN EASY EXIT — angle so an impact pushes the vehicle AWAY from where people are working · UPWIND AND UPHILL, and BEYOND spreading fluid · WARNING LIGHTS ON, but MORE IS NOT BETTER — drivers STEER TOWARDS WHAT THEY LOOK AT · HIGH-VISIBILITY ON EVERY ROADWAY INCIDENT — including daylight, including the two-minute ones, WHICH ARE THE ONES PEOPLE GET HIT ON · NEVER TURN YOUR BACK ON TRAFFIC · GET THE PATIENT OUT OF THE LANE AS SOON AS IT IS SAFE · LOAD FROM THE PROTECTED SIDE — the most exposed moment of the call · ASSUME THE WORST DRIVER ON THAT ROAD IS ABOUT TO ARRIVE
back.why_it_matters: The officer sent them back for the vest, and made a point of doing it in front of everyone.

back.body: REQUESTED WHERE FLYING MEANINGFULLY SHORTENS TIME TO DEFINITIVE CARE — COUNT THE WHOLE SEQUENCE HONESTLY: launch, flight in, landing, loading, flight out. Over a short distance A GROUND UNIT WITH THE PATIENT ALREADY LOADED USUALLY WINS · WEATHER AND AVAILABILITY REMOVE THE OPTION AT SHORT NOTICE — ALWAYS HAVE A GROUND PLAN · REQUEST EARLY; cancelling is cheap · LZ: FLAT, FIRM, CLEAR of wires, poles, trees, signs, fences, vehicles, people · WIRES ARE THE PRINCIPAL HAZARD AND ARE NEARLY INVISIBLE FROM THE AIR — REPORT THEM AND SAY WHERE · ROTOR WASH TURNS LOOSE MATERIAL INTO PROJECTILES — secure everything · NOBODY APPROACHES UNTIL SIGNALLED · APPROACH FROM THE FRONT, IN THE PILOT'S VIEW · NEVER FROM THE REAR — THE TAIL ROTOR IS INVISIBLE · ON A SLOPE, APPROACH DOWNHILL
back.why_it_matters: The pilot said afterwards that they would not have seen it.

back.body: BACK INJURY ENDS MORE EMS CAREERS THAN ANYTHING DRAMATIC — and it ACCUMULATES rather than arriving · LIFT WITH THE LEGS · BACK STRAIGHT (straight, not vertical) · BEND AT HIPS AND KNEES · NEVER TWIST UNDER LOAD — the spine takes compression well and ROTATION UNDER LOAD VERY BADLY. To change direction, MOVE YOUR FEET · KEEP THE WEIGHT CLOSE — DISTANCE MULTIPLIES the force on your spine, dramatically · FEET SHOULDER WIDTH, BALANCED, FIRM GRIP, PALMS UP · BRIEF THE LIFT · ONE PERSON CALLS IT and EVERYONE MOVES ON THAT COUNT — lifting a quarter-second apart means somebody took the whole weight · ASK FOR HELP BEFORE YOU START, not once committed · USE THE EQUIPMENT · PUSH RATHER THAN PULL · THE DANGER IS IN THE UNPLANNED MOMENTS
back.why_it_matters: For about a quarter of a second one person had most of the weight.

back.body: See the skill card steps. Critical: PLAN THE ROUTE, ASK FOR ENOUGH PEOPLE NOW, GET CLOSE BEFORE LIFTING, feet shoulder width with a firm grip, BEND AT HIPS AND KNEES WITH A STRAIGHT BACK, BRIEF THE LIFT OUT LOUD, ONE PERSON CALLS IT and everyone moves on that count, NEVER TWIST UNDER LOAD, KEEP IT CLOSE THROUGHOUT THE CARRY, and SLOW DOWN AT THE AWKWARD PARTS.
back.why_it_matters: The lift you planned for is not the one that hurts you. The corner is.

back.body: EMERGENCY MOVE: THE DANGER OF STAYING OUTWEIGHS THE RISK OF MOVING — and it ACCEPTS that you may worsen an injury · THREE REASONS ONLY: IMMEDIATE DANGER (fire, collapse, hazmat, traffic, water) · YOU CANNOT REACH ANOTHER PATIENT · THE CARE THEY NEED CANNOT BE GIVEN WHERE THEY ARE · DRAG ALONG THE LONG AXIS — clothes drag, blanket drag, shoulder or armpit drag · URGENT MOVE: the PATIENT'S CONDITION demands speed — rapid extrication is the example, and it is JUSTIFIED BY CONDITION, NOT BY AN AWKWARD CAR · NON-URGENT: planned, unhurried, device chosen, lift briefed — and THIS IS WHERE MOST BACK INJURIES HAPPEN, because it is where most of the lifting is · SPEED IS NEVER A JUSTIFICATION ON ITS OWN
back.why_it_matters: The officer asked what the patient's condition was. The honest answer was stable.

back.body: See the comparison rows: what justifies it, the three reasons, the risk accepted, spinal care, typical methods, planning, where injuries actually happen, and whether speed counts as a reason.
back.why_it_matters: An emergency move trades a risk of worse injury against a worse alternative. Nothing else does.

back.body: WHEELED STRETCHER — the default; LOADING HAS A KNOWN INJURY PATTERN, follow the procedure, especially on powered models · STAIR CHAIR — seated patient down stairs; REQUIRES SOMEONE WHO TOLERATES SITTING UP · SCOOP — SPLITS AND ASSEMBLES UNDERNEATH with minimal patient movement, no roll needed · LONG BOARD — AN EXTRICATION AND MOVEMENT DEVICE, NOT A TRANSPORT SURFACE; prolonged board time causes pain and pressure injury · VACUUM MATTRESS — conforms, spreads load, MUCH BETTER FOR LONG OR ROUGH JOURNEYS · BASKET — rough ground and technical rescue · FLEXIBLE — narrow, awkward spaces a rigid device will not turn · SLIDE SHEETS AND TRANSFER BOARDS — THE MOST UNDERUSED KIT IN THE SERVICE; they turn a LIFT into a SLIDE · EVERY DEVICE HAS A WEIGHT LIMIT AND A PROCEDURE
back.why_it_matters: Ninety seconds to fetch the slide sheet. Four seconds for the move, and nobody lifted anything.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-02-03. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: POSITION BY CONDITION — it is a CLINICAL DECISION, not a default · BREATHING DIFFICULTY → SIT THEM UP (often the single most effective thing you do) · REDUCED CONSCIOUSNESS BUT BREATHING → position to PROTECT THE AIRWAY so vomit comes OUT rather than IN · SHOCK → FOLLOW YOUR PROTOCOL; guidance has changed and varies · SECURE THE PATIENT TO THE DEVICE, THEN THE DEVICE TO THE VEHICLE — BOTH, EVERY TIME · STRAPS SNUG ENOUGH TO HOLD IN A SUDDEN STOP, and RECHECKED AFTER MOVING · STRAP THE LEGS TOO — patients SLIDE DOWNWARDS whenever the device tilts · COVER THEM AT EVERY STAGE — moving is when they are least covered and most exposed · KEEP TUBING AND LINES WHERE THEY CANNOT BE CAUGHT OR PULLED
back.why_it_matters: The stretcher had not latched, and nobody had heard it click.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-02-04. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: NOBODY APPROACHES UNTIL THE VEHICLE IS STABILISED AND THE HAZARDS ARE IDENTIFIED · A CAR ON ITS WHEELS CAN STILL ROLL, ROCK AND SETTLE — on its side or roof it is INHERENTLY UNSTABLE · TRAFFIC IS THE FIRST HAZARD at nearly every vehicle incident — the crash is stationary and the traffic is not · ENGINE OFF; BATTERY ISOLATED by trained personnel · UNDEPLOYED AIRBAGS ARE STORED EXPLOSIVE CHARGES THAT CAN FIRE LATE, EVEN AFTER POWER IS CUT — stay out of the path, and remember SIDE, CURTAIN AND KNEE BAGS · ELECTRIC AND HYBRID: high voltage, hazardous cabling, DELAYED REIGNITION — identify early and say so · DOWNED LINES: WHOLE AREA IS A NO-GO until the utility says dead; A LINE NEED NOT SPARK TO BE LIVE, and OCCUPANTS STAY IN THE VEHICLE · SIMPLE ACCESS = NO TOOLS: TRY EVERY DOOR · COMPLEX ACCESS BELONGS TO RESCUE
back.why_it_matters: Somebody walked round and tried the rear passenger door. It opened on the first pull.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-03-01. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: ONE PERSON COMMANDS THE INCIDENT, ONE PERSON IS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PATIENT — at a rescue you are usually the second · YOUR JOB IS THE PATIENT, NOT THE TOOLS — get in, stay in, keep working · TELL RESCUE WHAT THE CONDITION NEEDS: a STABLE patient buys them twenty tidy minutes; a DETERIORATING one changes the plan to fast and rough — AND ONLY YOU CAN TELL THEM WHICH · IF THEY WORSEN, SAY SO IMMEDIATELY. DO NOT WAIT TO BE ASKED · COVER AGAINST GLASS, DUST AND DEBRIS — FACE AND EYES · Hearing protection · KEEP THEM WARM: roof and doors off is long exposure · EXPLAIN EACH THING BEFORE IT HAPPENS — 'the next noise is the roof, it will be very loud' · MANUAL SPINAL STABILISATION per protocol · REASSESS ON A RHYTHM · OUT ALONG THE PATH OF LEAST HARM
back.why_it_matters: The plan changed inside twenty seconds, because somebody said it out loud and once.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-03-02. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: See the skill card steps. Critical: KNOW YOUR ROLE, THE PATIENT NOT THE TOOLS, manage airway and bleeding, MAINTAIN MANUAL SPINAL STABILISATION, TELL RESCUE WHAT THE CONDITION NEEDS, SAY IT IMMEDIATELY IF THEY DETERIORATE, COVER FACE AND EYES, KEEP THEM WARM, EXPLAIN BEFORE EACH LOUD THING, REASSESS ON A RHYTHM, and REMOVE ALONG THE PATH OF LEAST HARM.
back.why_it_matters: The people who could change the plan are outside the car holding equipment.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-03-02. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: A STANDARD STRUCTURE FOR ANY INCIDENT, from a two-car collision to a disaster · PURPOSE: ONE PLAN · CLEAR ROLES · A SPAN OF CONTROL A HUMAN CAN MANAGE · EXACTLY ONE PERSON IS IN COMMAND — identified, known, and TRANSFERRED FORMALLY when it changes. Command that drifts is command nobody holds · SPAN OF CONTROL ≈ 3 TO 7 (5 as the working number) — exceed it and you add a LAYER. That is arithmetic about attention, not bureaucracy · PLAIN LANGUAGE, NOT AGENCY CODES — your code may mean nothing to the fire crew on the same channel · UNIFIED COMMAND when an incident crosses agencies · YOU TAKE ASSIGNMENTS FROM ONE SUPERVISOR ONLY · REPORT IN → TAKE THE ASSIGNMENT → WORK IN IT → REPORT BACK · FREELANCING IS THE DANGER, and it is always well intentioned
back.why_it_matters: One name did not come back, and for ninety seconds nobody could say where he was.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-04-01. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: AN MCI IS PATIENTS EXCEEDING THE RESOURCES IMMEDIATELY AVAILABLE — RELATIVE, NOT A NUMBER. Three patients IS an MCI for one ambulance an hour from anywhere · THE FIRST UNIT SIZES UP, DECLARES, REQUESTS AND TAKES COMMAND — IT TREATS NOBODY. Start treating and you have removed the only person who could organise this · INITIAL REPORT: location · what happened · APPROXIMATE numbers · hazards · access. Rough and early beats accurate and late · REQUEST EARLY AND GENEROUSLY — cancelling is cheap, under-calling is not · ROLES BY FUNCTION: TRIAGE · TREATMENT · TRANSPORT · STAGING · STAGING stops units self-deploying and vanishing into the incident · RECORD WHO WENT WHERE — it cannot be reconstructed afterwards · THE AIM SHIFTS: THE MOST GOOD FOR THE MOST PATIENTS
back.why_it_matters: He walked past the man holding his arm. He said it was the hardest thirty seconds of his career.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-04-02. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: SIMPLE TRIAGE AND RAPID TREATMENT — BUILT TO BE FAST RATHER THAN RIGHT, and that trade is deliberate · SECONDS PER PATIENT, NOT MINUTES · ONLY THREE INTERVENTIONS: OPEN THE AIRWAY · CONTROL MAJOR BLEEDING · MOVE ON. Anything else means you have stopped triaging · 1. CAN THEY WALK? → MINOR. This one step often removes most of the problem in fifteen seconds · 2. BREATHING? If not, OPEN THE AIRWAY — breathing now = IMMEDIATE, still not = DECEASED · 3. RATE ABOVE 30? → IMMEDIATE · 4. NO RADIAL PULSE or REFILL OVER 2 SECONDS? → IMMEDIATE · 5. CANNOT FOLLOW A SIMPLE COMMAND? → IMMEDIATE, otherwise DELAYED · TRIAGE IS REPEATED — A TAG IS A SNAPSHOT, NOT A VERDICT
back.why_it_matters: Nineteen people stood up and walked to the fence. What was left was a problem you can work.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-04-03. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: Walk → MINOR. Not walking → breathing? Not breathing → open the airway → breathing = IMMEDIATE, still not = DECEASED. Breathing → rate above 30 = IMMEDIATE → no radial pulse or refill over 2 seconds = IMMEDIATE → cannot follow commands = IMMEDIATE, can follow = DELAYED. Control major bleeding when you find it.
back.why_it_matters: Three interventions only. Airway, bleeding, move on.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-04-03. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: THE PAEDIATRIC VERSION, because CHILDREN ARREST FROM RESPIRATORY CAUSES — an apnoeic child may have a perfectly good heart that just needs air · Looks like a child, use JumpSTART; looks like an adult, use START. Do not deliberate · WALKING → MINOR — but INFANTS TOO YOUNG TO WALK ARE CARRIED THERE AND ASSESSED, because the walking logic does not apply to someone who never walked · NOT BREATHING → OPEN THE AIRWAY → breathing = IMMEDIATE · STILL NOT BREATHING → CHECK A PULSE: NO PULSE = DECEASED · PULSE BUT NO BREATHING → GIVE FIVE RESCUE BREATHS — THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT OF JUMPSTART · Breathing after = IMMEDIATE, still apnoeic = DECEASED · RATE BELOW 15 OR ABOVE 45 = IMMEDIATE (slow matters as much as fast) · NO PERIPHERAL PULSE = IMMEDIATE · AVPU: POSTURING OR UNRESPONSIVE = IMMEDIATE, otherwise DELAYED
back.why_it_matters: The child was breathing by the fourth one.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-04-04. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: Walk → MINOR (infants too young to walk are carried there and assessed). Not breathing → open the airway → breathing = IMMEDIATE; still not → pulse? No pulse = DECEASED; pulse present → FIVE RESCUE BREATHS → breathing = IMMEDIATE, still apnoeic = DECEASED. Breathing → rate below 15 or above 45 = IMMEDIATE → no peripheral pulse = IMMEDIATE → AVPU: posturing or unresponsive = IMMEDIATE, otherwise DELAYED.
back.why_it_matters: Pulse but no breathing means five breaths. That is the difference.

back.body: THE MOST DANGEROUS HAZMAT INCIDENT IS THE ONE NOBODY RECOGNISED — crews walk in, treat patients, and BECOME patients · RECOGNISE FROM A DISTANCE: UPWIND, UPHILL, WELL BACK, THROUGH BINOCULARS — which exist so that reading a placard never requires being close enough for it to matter · CLUES: the OCCUPANCY · CONTAINER SHAPE · PLACARDS AND LABELS · spilled liquid, vapour clouds, unexplained fog, bubbling, DEAD OR DISTRESSED VEGETATION, INSECTS AND ANIMALS · AND THE ONE MOST OFTEN MISSED: SEVERAL PEOPLE WITH THE SAME SYMPTOMS IN THE SAME PLACE — hazmat until proved otherwise, and it presents as medicine · NO ODOUR PROVES NOTHING — many are odourless, some destroy your sense of smell, and if you CAN smell it you are IN it · YOUR JOB: RECOGNISE · RETREAT · ISOLATE · NOTIFY
back.why_it_matters: Somebody stopped at the top of the stairs and said the word out loud. None of them became the fifth.

back.body: WHITE (front and back) — how to use it and what to do first · YELLOW — by FOUR-DIGIT UN NUMBER · BLUE — by NAME · ORANGE — the GUIDE PAGES: fire, spill, first aid, protective clothing · GREEN — INITIAL ISOLATION AND PROTECTIVE ACTION DISTANCES.
back.why_it_matters: Yellow by number · Blue by name · Orange for what to do · Green for how far back.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-05-01. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: THREE ZONES, AND THE DIVISION IS WHAT STOPS A CONTAINED INCIDENT SPREADING · HOT ZONE: contains the hazard; ONLY TRAINED, PROTECTED PERSONNEL; NO PATIENT CARE BEYOND GETTING THEM OUT — no assessment, no vital signs · WARM ZONE: THE DECONTAMINATION CORRIDOR — contamination reduced, PPE removed IN SEQUENCE; life-saving intervention only, by trained protected people · COLD ZONE: command, staging, TREATMENT, transport, the ambulances — NOTHING CONTAMINATED ENTERS · MOVEMENT IS ONE WAY: HOT → WARM → COLD, never back without reprocessing · EMTs WORK IN THE COLD ZONE unless specifically trained and equipped · BOUNDARIES ARE SET BY HAZARD, WIND AND TERRAIN — IF THE WIND SHIFTS, THE ZONES MOVE, INCLUDING WHERE YOU PARKED · CONTAMINATED PATIENTS NEVER ENTER THE AMBULANCE
back.why_it_matters: Moving the treatment area cost them eight minutes and saved them everything else.

front.title: Hot zone vs warm zone
front.summary: And where the cold zone sits

back.body: See the comparison rows: what each zone is, who enters, what patient care is permitted, what happens there, whether an EMT works there, direction of movement, what sets the boundary, and the cold zone that lies beyond both.
back.why_it_matters: Hot, warm, cold, one way only. Every shortcut across a boundary makes the incident bigger.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-05-02. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: REMOVING THE CLOTHING IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE STEP — no equipment, seconds, and MOST OF WHAT LANDED ON THEM IS ON THEIR CLOTHES · DRY FIRST, THEN WET: BRUSH OR BLOT DRY POWDERS OFF BEFORE ANY WATER — some materials REACT with water, and wetting can spread it or drive it into skin · THEN COPIOUS WATER, HEAD DOWNWARDS, protecting the AIRWAY AND EYES · BAG, ISOLATE AND RECORD clothing and belongings — they may identify the substance · DECONTAMINATE BEFORE THE AMBULANCE, NEVER IN IT — an interior cannot be decontaminated, and you would produce a contaminated vehicle, crew and hospital bay · PROTECT YOURSELF FIRST: a contaminated responder treats nobody and becomes a patient · SECONDARY ROUTES: skin, clothing, hair, belongings, VOMIT · RUNOFF IS CONTAMINATED TOO
back.why_it_matters: The guidebook entry, read afterwards, said the material reacted with water.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-05-03. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: RESPONDERS ARE DELIBERATELY TARGETED HERE — the danger is aimed at YOU, not incidental · RECOGNISE: the EVENT (explosion, shooting, vehicle attack) · the TARGET (symbolic, crowded, significant date) · UNUSUAL DEVICES · MULTIPLE BLAST OR PENETRATING INJURIES somewhere that should not produce them · SECONDARY DEVICES ARE PLACED WHERE RESPONDERS WILL GATHER, TIMED FOR WHEN THEY ARRIVE — the instinct to converge and park close is the behaviour being exploited · DO NOT ENTER UNTIL DECLARED SECURE BY THE AGENCY RESPONSIBLE — not when it looks quiet, not when you can see casualties · STAGE AWAY, OUT OF SIGHT, AND AWAY FROM THE PREDICTABLE PLACES · DO NOT TOUCH OR INVESTIGATE ANYTHING UNUSUAL — report it · WORK INSIDE THE UNIFIED PLAN · PRESERVE THE SCENE, BUT PATIENT CARE WINS WHEN THEY CONFLICT
back.why_it_matters: If it is the obvious place, somebody else has thought of it too.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-06-01. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: CHEMICAL · BIOLOGICAL · RADIOLOGICAL · NUCLEAR · EXPLOSIVE · EXPLOSIVE IS BY FAR THE COMMONEST — blast injury is what you will actually see · CHEMICAL ACTS FAST: MANY CASUALTIES AT ONCE, ONE PLACE, SIMILAR SYMPTOMS — people collapsing in a confined space is chemical until proved otherwise, AND GOING IN IS HOW THE COUNT RISES · NERVE AGENTS: WET FROM EVERY ORIFICE AT ONCE, pinpoint pupils, difficulty breathing, twitching, seizures — recognition and protection are your part · BIOLOGICAL ACTS SLOWLY AND HAS NO SCENE — illness over hours or days, across a city. EMS MAY BE FIRST TO NOTICE THE PATTERN: say it out loud · RADIOLOGICAL: blast plus contamination · TIME · DISTANCE · SHIELDING · RADIATION IS NOT CONTAGIOUS — irradiated but uncontaminated patients are SAFE TO TREAT
back.why_it_matters: That sentence at handover, and not any clinical finding, was what started the investigation.

cards.verify_notes: Drafted from standard EMT curriculum (AAOS Emergency Care 12e level) and not yet reviewed against a source text, same as its parent concept EMT-08-06-02. Check every figure on this card against the source before it is printed or drilled.

back.body: A DISASTER OVERWHELMS THE AREA'S RESOURCES FOR A PROLONGED PERIOD — and PROLONGED is the word that changes everything · An MCI is a sprint that finishes. THIS DOES NOT · SHIFTS, RELIEFS, FOOD, WATER, SLEEP, FUEL AND RESUPPLY BECOME PART OF THE PLAN · NORMAL SYSTEMS FAIL: communications, power, water, roads — AND THE HOSPITALS THEMSELVES · EXPECT AUSTERE CONDITIONS, unfamiliar partners, improvised arrangements, decisions on less information · YOUR FAMILY'S PREPAREDNESS IS PART OF YOUR READINESS — you cannot work while worrying about them · PACE YOURSELF: the flat-out first sixteen hours buys you three useless days. EXHAUSTED RESPONDERS MAKE ERRORS AND GET HURT · EAT, DRINK, REST, HAND OVER — OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS · THE PSYCHOLOGICAL IMPACT CAN ARRIVE DAYS OR WEEKS LATER · KNOW THE SUPPORT BEFORE YOU NEED IT, AND WATCH YOUR COLLEAGUES
back.why_it_matters: At hour six it looks like commitment.
